absent: Full layouts of CPU signature, Intel header, extended table, early data, firmware and CPIO records beyond field uses visible here
Numeric values of MSR identifiers, NMI vector, header and checksum sizes, default total size and loader and header version constants
AMD early and late loading steps, blob format and validation beyond vendor gating and empty fallback
Initrd image path string, search mechanics and builtin firmware store implementation
Contents and callbacks of microcode operations table including apply, stage, finalize and flag meanings
Late load trigger, capability snapshot comparison, revision bookkeeping and error propagation outside stopped-CPU routine
Topology, APIC, CPU mask and stop-machine primitives used for rendezvous

findings.text: BSP early microcode entry parses command line, checks loader disable and CPU capability, records hypervisor presence, gates by vendor and family, then delegates to vendor specific BSP routine with shared early data.
AP entry skips when global disable flag set, reads vendor and family, invokes vendor AP routine only when family meets minimum, otherwise does nothing.

Intel BSP wrapper obtains blob, records old revision, attempts early application and on success marks global patch indicator and records new revision; AP and reload wrappers reuse that global indicator if present and reapply without rescanning.

Late loading entered via stopped-CPU callback that either arms per-CPU NMI enable and self targets, or calls update path directly; NMI handlers check enable flag, clear it, then dispatch to primary or secondary logic based on stored control CPU identity; offline handler additionally records offline result and joins rendezvous.

Per-CPU control holds a wait or apply or done directive, a result code, an identity of controlling CPU, and a boolean gating NMI handling; globals include a static key for NMI path, two rendezvous counters, a calibrated busy loop count, and a mask of soft-offlined members.

Early phase keeps a per-CPU array of CPU info structures, a small table of final revision identifiers terminated by zero, a single shared early data record for old and new revisions, and a device placeholder for late staging.

All participants first join a shared arrival counter with timeout; primaries apply patch then publish apply-or-done directive to siblings depending on success; secondaries wait for directive then either apply themselves or copy primary result and announce completion; CPU zero also kicks and later releases soft-offlined members via NMI.

Absent patch yields not-found; current revision at or above candidate yields already-current without hardware write and updates stored revision; otherwise hardware update is attempted and verified, yielding updated on match else error.

A candidate matches when its main signature equals collected CPU signature and platform mask overlaps, with empty mask treated as universal; otherwise extended table is examined entry by entry under same rule when present.

Scan walks concatenated images using declared total size or a default when data size empty, stops at first malformed or truncated entry, keeps only matching and erratum-safe candidates, and retains the highest revision newer than current in normal mode or exactly equal to current in save mode, returning nothing unless walk consumed whole buffer.

Validation rejects data extending beyond total, loader or header version mismatch, truncated or size-mismatched extended table, nonzero checksums over extended table words and over header plus data words, and per-entry extended checksum mismatch.

For a specific Granite Rapids family and model with stepping 1 and platform mask 0x95, revisions jumping over 0x1000405 from below are refused with a one-time diagnostic, all other combinations allowed.

Blob acquisition first collects CPU identity then prefers built-in firmware named by family and model and stepping on 64-bit, falling back to initrd path; total length comes from header totalsize when data size nonzero else a default constant; extended table length derives from entry count.
Early reload re-reads vendor and family and calls vendor reload only above same family minima as boot; family helper queries CPUID leaf one with zero subleaf.

Late update runs with CPUs stopped and uses atomic arrival counters plus per-CPU directives with bounded spinning and watchdog touches; staging asserts CPUs held and runs once per package over primary threads; non-instrumentable regions bracket instrumentable sections around prints, panic and watchdog.

Late arrival timeout marks timeout result and aborts batch; secondary wait failure for primary triggers panic as non-recoverable; incomplete or unsafe late load taints kernel out-of-spec; offline non-response and generic failures return IO error after counting updated and sibling and timeout and offline and failed buckets.

Staging aborts with diagnostic when image length misaligned, when mailbox read fails, or when per-package staging fails; late path still proceeds without staged image to reduce rendezvous time when possible.
Intel requires family at least 6, AMD family at least 0x10; CPUID leaf 1 EAX supplies family, ECX bit 31 records hypervisor presence.

Early parser looks for microcode option with comma separated suboptions force_minrev and dis_ucode_ldr plus debug-only hexadecimal base_rev, and also honors standalone boolean dis_ucode_ldr for compatibility; loader disable short-circuits both BSP and AP paths.

Final level table holds three revision identifiers followed by zero terminator; rendezvous spins up to one second with microsecond granularity and per-microsecond loop calibration, offline kick waits half that; Intel update uses write MSR and staging mailbox MSR with NMI vector and package scope.
Table entries are hex 0x01000098 then 0x0100009f then 0x010000af then zero marking end.
When vendor support not built, BSP and AP and reload helpers for both vendors are empty inline no-ops taking same parameters but performing no action.
